Diego: Quick follow-up from the Q&A: when you say "serving > model ownership" in terms of go-to-market, what should sales lean into on calls?

Elena (CEO): We should lead with measurable customer outcomes: lower $/M tokens, predictable p99, and simple fallbacks. Stop promising model X will solve everything. Instead: "we reliably serve the right model variant under your latency and cost constraints."

Diego: Can we put three quick bullets for customer decks?

Maya (VP Product): Sure: 1) Consistent latency at scale (p50/p95/p99) 2) Transparent unit economics (cost per 1k tokens, per-route) 3) Operational controls (rollouts, canary, private options). Keep it short.

Anya (Research): From a tech POV we should explain why this matters: model differences are incremental, but serving chops compound across usage. A 2x cut in per-token cost means customers can run experiments they otherwise wouldn't.

Ravi (CTO): Add: our runtime picks kernels by workload pattern, does continuous batching, and keeps KV caches warm across requests. That's what turns model capability into predictable product experience.

Ken (Solutions): Prospect question: how do we compare to CloudVendorA and ModelAPI-B? They both brag about model catalogs.

Elena (CEO): High-level battle-card line: CloudVendorA = model breadth + infra lock-in; ModelAPI-B = simple access, variable economics. Our counter: unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, measurable economics, and enterprise controls.

Diego: Any phrasing for objections about "we can just self-host open models cheaper"?

Ravi (CTO): Short answer: you can self-host but you pay ops tax and lose predictable unit economics and the SLO guarantees. Our selling points: startup friction removed, optimized kernels, and multi-tenant learnings that reduce cost.

Anya (Research): Also note: quantization/8-bit optimizations alone often require runtime-level tweaks to avoid generation artifacts. We can demonstrate a before/after quality metric on a prompt set.

Maya (VP Product): Product note: Sales want two artifacts: 1) a one-pager positioning statement with 3 competitor comparisons, 2) a small FAQ addressing "self-host vs Redwood" and "why not just pick the biggest model".

Elena (CEO): Actionable timeline: Ken to draft sales one-pager by Tue COB. Ravi and Anya to supply a short technical proof (benchmarks + one prompt eval) by Wed. Maya to assemble FAQ by Thu. I'll review on Thu afternoon.

Diego: Can we get a short script for SDRs? A 30s opener that foregrounds economics and reliability.

Maya (VP Product): Draft SDR script: "We help engineering teams cut inference costs and stabilize latency so features launch reliably — with Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments. Curious if predictable latency or lower token cost is a bigger priority for you?"

Diego: Nice. Will circulate.

Ken (Solutions): One more ask from enterprise AE: customers want examples of multi-region failover. Anyone we can point to as an architecture doc?

Ravi (CTO): Not public yet. I'll share an internal architecture note showing smart routing + region fallback patterns by end of week.

Elena (CEO): Perfect. Remember: our external messaging should be measurable and operational. Avoid generic "best models" language. Use concrete numbers and concise comparisons.
